Maths AA HL

Taylor / Maclaurin series

AHL 5.19 · math/taylor-series

The hard bit

You can compute the coefficients, but it is not obvious why adding terms helps, or why the approximation collapses far from the centre.

What this shows

The polynomial is built up one term at a time against sin(x). Each new term grips the curve over a wider interval, and outside that interval it shoots off to infinity - which is what radius of convergence means, visually.

Try changing

  • `FUNCTION` - one line: `"sin(x)"`, `"cos(x)"`, `"e^x"` or `"ln(1+x)"`. The last one has radius of convergence 1 (it converges for -1 < x <= 1); the shaded band shows where, and past x = 1 more terms make things worse.
  • `MAX_TERMS` - how many non-zero terms to build up to.
  • Add your own entry to `SERIES`, e.g. the geometric series 1/(1-x) = 1 + x + x² + ... (`term=lambda k: (1, k)`, `radius=1`).

The maths

f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(0)}{n!}\,x^n — Maclaurin series: a Taylor series centred on x = 0

\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{3!} + \frac{x^5}{5!} - \cdots — Only odd powers appear, so n non-zero terms reach x to the power 2n - 1

\ln(1+x) = x - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{3} - \cdots \qquad (-1 < x \le 1) — Radius of convergence 1: no number of terms works beyond x = 1

Check yourself

With sin(x) selected, will the 10-term polynomial stay within 0.05 of the curve for a whole wave either side of 0 (out to x = 2π ≈ 6.3)? Predict, then drag Terms to 10.

Yes, and a bit more: the readout says it tracks sin(x) from about x = -7.5 to 7.5. The series for sin(x) converges for every x, so each extra term pushes that edge further out; with 5 terms the edge is only at about 3.7.

Select ln(1+x). At x = 2, does going from 5 terms to 10 terms bring the polynomial closer to the curve, or send it further away?

Further away. At x = 2 the 5-term polynomial gives about 5.1 and the 10-term one about -64.8, against ln 3 ≈ 1.1. x = 2 is outside the radius of convergence (1), where the terms 2ⁿ/n grow instead of shrinking, so every term added makes it worse. Inside the shaded band the opposite happens: with 10 terms the readout's good region reaches x = 1.
